page_content: Benjamin's Journal
Entry 1:
I have caught wind of the ultimate prize - a blessing beyond any treasure even!
It holds secrets that no mortal would have any right to know, it holds the plans for a contraption that can bestow the touch of a God upon any ordinary quest! A blessing of fortune!
A tribute is needed, or so I would guess, but the tribute is the least of my concerns. For now I am after the instructions.
Entry 2:
It would seem that the pieces I need were on this very land. There more proof to justify my search than there is to condemn it. I shall meander with purpose, I think.
Entry 3:
I have been through many of the chasms in this place. Through moldy dungeons and man-made pits of filth and for my efforts I have found nothing.
I have narrowed my area of interest down as a consolation, though! It is not buried deep within the soil, no, on the contrary, it is exactly the opposite!

It is in The Planes! It was gifted to Fernalla and Vitheo and in some act of desperation, it seems they broke it in two and cast it into their planar waters to be forever lost to man and beast. How unlikely that any who tread there would think to cast a line with so many forces pulling their curiosity in other directions
Entry 4:
I have studied my notes, and I am confident that if presented with the two halves, I could piece them back together!
Wardens of the Northern Veil
There is little left to occupy the hours in what feel like our final days. We are sealed within the hills, prisoners of the beast that fell from the stars.
I suspect that anyone who finds these pages will dismiss them as tavern fiction. Still, I have nothing left but time, and so I write.
Our people are not Paladins. My brothers seem to be forgetting who they were, but for some cruel reason that mercy has not been given to me. I remember myself. I know what I am.

My ancestors came from the south of Erenshor like all others. But while Brax’s attention lay elsewhere, Sivakaya took a group of our people by their hands, and she guided us quietly through forest and hill, urging silence as we went north, further than any had gone before.

She told us the veil between this world and the Void was thin, that darkness bled through unseen seams in this place. Our people were warned not to interfere. They were asked only to watch, to stand guard against the things that might crawl into being.

To further secure our mission, Sivakaya, in her teachings at the Duskenlight school where magic was first given freely to the world, spoke often of the North. She cautioned her students away from our place, saying wisdom lay in remaining south, far from the corruption that lingered there.

Living beside that power was never easy. Over generations, it shaped us in ways of which Sivakaya never warned. Our people first learned to endure it, then to coexist with it, and eventually they learned to draw strength from it.

They discovered that it could not be driven back or denied. Those who hungered for more than was offered were twisted into abominations and had to be destroyed. Those who declined its gift were driven mad. So we learned restraint. We accepted what came, never refused it, and never asked for more.
We built a life there. We watched the roads. We turned travelers away. And we became Reavers, guardians of the Darkness who protect the Darkness from the world, and the world from the Darkness.
But everything changed when the sorcerer arrived.

He claimed the southern schools had taught him all they could. He said the Duskenlight held no more answers, and he begged us to teach him the truths of the North. He said he was there with the blessing of Sivakaya herself.
He learned quickly, but patience never took root in him. The pace of the Void’s offerings frustrated him. He wanted more than it would give, and when denied, he took it for himself.
One night he stepped through a door that would never open again. His body remained on Erenshor, but its insides were twisted and wrong.
He was what needed to be destroyed. He was what Sivakaya warned us might crawl from the seams of that Void. We failed.
The Void magnified his natural power, and he was far too strong to restrain. He left our city, and we never heard from him again.
Nearly five centuries passed. Our people continued on their mission of protection in silence.

Then the sky caught fire. The world shook. A mass of stone the size of a mountain was flung into the skies and fell southward in fire and ruin for days and days. We set out at once to reach Brax’s people and Sivakaya’s faithful to ensure they were intact.
Along the road we found camps of refugees who told of slaughter and loss, but none could explain the burning sky or falling stone. So we turned our expedition toward its origin.
That was when we met Soluna.

She loomed over us. Her physical presence was impressive, but standing alongside her was like standing within the heavens. We could sense the presence of knowledge that would not fit within our own minds.

Soluna sensed the divinity bound within us. She sensed the Void as well. Seeing an opportunity to gain a foothold on Erenshor, she bound us in her own power, reshaping us into something that served her design. The Void was torn from us and cast away by the force of the stars.
Her voice came as echoes. She told us we would claim this world in her name, that we would shepherd Erenshor into a golden age. She expected our thanks for her gift.
We refused. We did not thank her.

Our identities had already been stolen, and we would not give her our will as well. We swore we would never serve her, and that the truth of her domination would endure beyond us, and that her name would be forever known as one to be feared.
She answered with anger. Many of us fled into the mountains and hid there for a time.

Still, she called to us through the stars each night, promising love and mercy, promising release from this place. Those weak enough to listen wandered toward her light in the dark hours of night. Many were lost to us. Those she claimed carried her doctrine across the land, laying the foundations of the Paladins.
Those of us who remained prayed for her end.
It came at last. Astra arrived, and the heavens burned with war until Soluna withdrew. Astra, broken and spent, scattered herself into stardust along the crater’s edge.
We believed hope had died with her. Instead, our despair fed Astra’s rebirth. Any who left this place were drawn into her, consumed to restore what she had lost.
The guardians of Soluna did nothing to free us. We were a threat to the faith she left behind, and so we were allowed to rot in silence.
And so, this is the place where we are forever lost.
The Malaroth Ledger

'Too dangerous' is all they say. The weak ones do, at least. Men and their meddling - despite their lack of rank amongst us and wearing their lack of conviction on their sleeves, they beg me to stop. They see a friend perish, I see a stepping stone to a better future for all of us. Our success will be mapped by the bloody footprints we leave as we push forward. Our legacy is forged in sacrifice. Thankfully, it was theirs.

Undeniably, exporting these creatures to Mersoavilla will offer the best chance for profit. Imagine, our ships glide into the Merosavilla Docks with cages prominently placed on the decks containing the stomping beasts. Picture the banners flying over us as we parade the monsters through the city - docile and tame. If fortune favors, we might even demonstrate their might on a captive for the crowd to see. To cement the value of what we bring.

I admit, the learning curve has been steep. We’ve lost a few good men - well, men, at least. None are definable as ‘good’ when compared to the cunning of a woman. It seems these beasts have a knack for sniffing out fear and weakness. The timid handlers don’t last. It’s poetic, in a way. I have no desire for cowards in my crew, and neither do the Malaroths.
Then there’s the feed. Measured and precise it attracts them as reliably as a corpse attracts flies. The same temperament.  The same movements. Predictable. But changing one thing changes everything.

A Moongill. The elusive little night-fish. Malaroths love them. But when it’s mixed with our feed recipe, something changes. The predictable ones shy away, and something else approaches. It’s shaped like a Malaroth but it acts like a shadow wrapped in flesh. Its eyes contain a craze, its breaths seem to emit a dark fog, and its movements are sporadic. Faster. Meaner. There’s something primal and ancient about its presence.

For now we will stay measured. The moongill feed is prohibited, and it cannot be brought anywhere near the dish. Not until we can prepare more. There’s no question the true power lies in the darker beasts, but we have no power over them. With plans in place, the orders will come flooding in. Bags of gold. Promises of power, connections, and wealth. My name will be spoken with respect and I will get used to it.

To ensure the affliction we’ve seen in some does not spread to all, it is imperative that we move our operations to Mersovilla. Seeded by healthy speciments, we can continue uninterrupted and unimpeded. I cannot risk the darkness becoming prevalent within my herd. I wonder if it was placed there by this land itself or something worse. I wish not to find out.

The crew is restless, as they always are, but dreams of fortune are dancing and hopes of home are becoming real. They see it - fortune and glory. They feel it. The Malaroths are our ticket and I’ll see that none stand in our way. Some will call me ruthless. Some will call me brilliant. Both will be correct. My name will be carved into Erenshor history, and with these beasts by my side, the world will kneel in my wake.
Godless Amarion

Sivakaya had recognized Azynthi’s extraordinary talent from the moment he set foot upon her school’s ancient stone walkways. Through his lessons, she witnessed his power take hold of him in a way it does for only the most gifted arcanists. His eyes flowed to and fro, as though energized by a presence of mana itself, and the world seemed to bend to his very thoughts as he passed through the hallowed stone halls of that place.

Upon completing his training, Azynthi began to seek additional knowledge on his own accord, setting off to explore the northern country in search of greater answers. Sivakaya and Brax did not often discuss what lay beyond the Twin Soldiers, but as the architects of those places and the rest of Amarion, they undoubtedly understood the dangers Azynthi might face. Whether they believed he was equipped to navigate those challenges or were unaware of the extent of the creeping corruption overtaking that region, they allowed Azynthi to wander into something far darker than he was prepared to handle.

It is known that upon creating Amarion, Sivakaya and Brax buried a balancing darkness deep within the planet’s crust to allow further prosperity and growth to flourish unobstructed across the surface. Humanity across Erenshor and Merosavilla thrived as a result, but the obscured north of Erenshor remained uninhabited. Whether by divine intention or sheer chance, it was ultimately best that humans did not tread there.

Azynthi’s foray into that place remains largely undocumented. However, his return is sparsely noted in Siva-Braxonian writings. He was markedly changed: quiet and pensive, lurking at the periphery of society, eventually retreating to a small island east of Braxonia where he made a solitary home.

When Sivakaya experienced a vision of great pain descending upon Erenshor, she sought Azynthi’s counsel. He spoke to her in hushed tones, sharing secrets that even she, as an Elder Goddess, had not known prior but recognized to be true. He revealed that he had encountered something in the north that would not ever reveal itself to her, and that a new power now coursed through him-a power he could share with her.

Azynthi promised her the means to repel any forces that might threaten her beloved people. He warned repeatedly of a creeping horror beyond the Twin Soldiers, a culmination of buried secrets and torment-a blight of sorrow and despair, and hordes of terrible devil-things that walked amongst the shadows there. He claimed that even a goddess could not stand against it alone.

Brax tried to dissuade Sivakaya from accepting Azynthi’s offer, warning her of a darkness within him that absorbed even the brightest flame. Azynthi’s eyes no longer flowed bright with an arcane gift - they were deadened and muted as though some unseeable shroud has been pulled across them. Sivakaya promised Brax she would not accept the gift, but ultimately, she broke her word.

Azynthi and Sivakaya performed the ritual in secret on the outskirts of Braxonia. As lights and bolts swirled around them, a cold northern wind swept across the field blowing away any sensation of warmth and sweeping shadow over the light. Sivakaya felt herself shrink deep within her own body, overwhelmed by an encroaching darkness. With a flourish of unknown magic, Azynthi absorbed the darkness back from her and with it, the very essence of Sivakaya herself, leaving her an empty husk, stripped of compassion, love, empathy, and agency.

Azynthi, standing opposite a newly-formed monolith of corruption that materialized from the sheer energy of the massive disturbance, basked in his success. The power of a goddess coursed through him, but his unveiled corruption was now undeniable. The blighted winds he had summoned carried a darkness to the surrounding land, infecting it. Animals and people alike grew mad, violent, and uncontrollable.
Sivakaya vanished for decades with many of her followers in tow.

In Sivakaya’s absence, the monolith of corruption formed by their ritual began to leak upon the land, spreading its disease as though it were flowing mud, creeping across hills and homes alike. Many citizens recoiled and left their homes, and those who stayed were overtaken by an incurable madness and a desire for destruction.

When Sivakaya and her followers re-emerged from their seclusion, it was as twisted and demonic figures, driven by greed and selfishness but determined to prepare for the creeping horror that Sivakaya had foreseen. Many of her followers embraced the corruption, some worshipping her in darkened churches guarded by demonic figures, while others donned black armor and roamed the land, seeking threats to destroy in their demented fervor.

Brax, upon Sivakaya’s new shape, in a fit of despair and enraged at Azynthi, smote the land and the monolith to stop the corruption from spreading further, creating a vast desert to contain the spreading blight. His sacrifice buried his own glorious city and people beneath the sands, ultimately saving the continent of Erenshor from certain doom.

Some amongst Sivakaya’s former followers had seen her new form for the tragedy it was. Led by Eldrin Shadowmire, they called themselves “The Wisp,” and they pulled away from their Goddess instead of following her, and they retreated into the Loomingwood Forest. There, they warded against Sivakaya’s presence and began researching ways to restore her to her former self in secrecy.

Upon Eldrin, Brax bestowed the Nighthollow Candle, lit by a flame ignited by Brax himself. He told them this candle would illuminate past memories of Sivakaya, and urged them to find a way to reverse her corruption.
War began as Brax’s followers clashed with the corrupted and broken Sivakayans. The children of Brax and Sivakaya - Vitheo and Fernalla - abandoned their mother and fought against her alongside Brax.

After years of conflict to salvage Amarion, culminating in a Braxonian victory to repel Sivakaya to the North, Brax’s win did not come without further tragedy-his children Fernalla and Vitheo were both felled through battle or treachery, and though their demises resulted in an ascent to divinity, Brax mourned their losses.

Brax had become angry and distant, all but abandoning the land. The world he and Sivakaya had created as a beacon of light and hope was eclipsed by Sivakaya’s embodiment of darkness. Brax’s people lay buried beneath the sands, and Sivakaya’s followers were ruined by her curse. Unable to bear further sight of their crumbling shared creation, Brax turned away, leaving the world to its fate.
Strange Beasts of Erenshor

The lands of Erenshor are vast and brimming with life. From the towering peaks of the Sivakayan Spine to the wind-swept plains of Fernalla’s Revival Plains, countless creatures roam. Some are known to the denizens of the land, while others remain hidden, as if cloaked by the very gods who shaped this world.

In the Duskenlight forests, tales speak of Giant Men who tread softly but leave imprints the size of kite shields. Meanwhile, Silkengrass Meadow has seen fleeting appearances of the Albino Kodiak, a spectral predator whispered to bring luck or doom, depending on the intent of the observer.

Yet, not all beasts that haunt Erenshor's whispers have been seen by mortal eyes. Ancient texts, etched in the forgotten halls of Brax's old libraries, hint at a beast that roams The Brake under the pale moonlight. This creature, described as 'a demon of flesh and shadow,' is said to linger near the swampy heart of the woods, where the waters do not churn.

Travelers passing near the region are warned to tread lightly, for the beast is as dangerous as it is rare. Should one encounter it, the only prudent course is to flee, for courage is no match for its primal fury. It is worth noting though, that accounts are untrustworthy and out of many legends, this one may be least likely to carry truth.

While some dismiss all tales as mere folklore, the history of Erenshor has proven time and again that truth and legend often itermingle in unexpected ways. The land keeps its secrets well, burying them in ancient ruins and forgotten groves and shrouding them in dangerous shadow. Who is to say what might lie beyond the veil of common knowledge?

To those who dare to wander with open eyes and a curious heart, Erenshor offers things unseen by others. And should luck - or perhaps the gods - favor your journey, you might find yourself face to face with one of its many wonders. Whether you survive the encounter, however, is a tale only time will tell.
The Construction of Port Azure

The construction of Port Azure marked a turning point in the history of Erenshor. Following the arrival of the Solunarian Paladins, the scattered settlements of the continent began working toward the creation of a unified capital. Their efforts accelerated after the discovery of a remarkable crater in the northern reaches of the continent. Hidden beneath a shrine to Soluna and guarded by what contemporary accounts described as 'monstrous but benign golems,' the site was identified as Soluna's Landing, a place regarded as having immense religious and historical importance.

The Solunarian Paladins quickly claimed the site and declared Erenshor to be a holy land. Although a small native population already inhabited the region, the newcomers regarded their way of life as primitive. The Fernallan druids lived in tents and simple wooden shelters, while many Braxonians were said to display signs of severe mental decline that local traditions attributed to an ancient catastrophe. Some accounts describe a divine event in which an entire civilization was destroyed in an outpouring of sorrow from the gods. These stories, however, have nevr been verified and are generally regarded as legend.

To support the growing settlement, the Paladins organized the arrival of colonists from across the known world, including Fernallan, Braxonian, and Vithean communities, primarily from Merosavilla. Many believed they were settling land once touched by the gods themselves. Construction of the city began in the year 1552 and continued steadily for nearly a century and a half. Port Azure was officially completed in the year 1700, an occasion celebrated throughout the region.

During the city's construction, a section of the castle unexpectedly collapsed. The original purpose of this section has been lost to history, and surviving records offer few details. Later rumors claimed the area had once housed imprisoned Sivakayan agents under the watch of the Azure Guard, but no evidence has been found to support these stories. At the time, Sivakayans were widely considered little more than figures of folklore rather than a genuine threat.

Administrative control of the growing city eventually passed to the Government of Merosavilla, whose resources had funded much of the settlement effort. Under Merosavillan leadership, the Azure Guard was established to maintain law and protect the city. As the population grew, Port Azure attracted merchants, craftsmen, and travelers from many cultures, developing into the continent's leading and only center of commerce. Its natural harbor further strengthened its importance as a major hub of maritime trade across the world.

The Azure Guard became known for its strict enforcement of the law. Pirates, brigands, and other individuals considered threats to public order were expelled from the city or sentenced to death. While some citizens privately criticized these harsh measures, particularly in taverns and other informal gatherings, no organized opposition is known to have emerged.

Today, Port Azure stands as the most influential city in Erenshor. Its strategic harbor, thriving markets, and enduring military presence continue to secure its position as a center of trade and government. With the Azure Guard maintaining order, most scholars believe the city is well positioned to remain prosperous for generations to come.
The Fall of Rockshade Hold

Once a haven of silent scholars, Rockshade Hold now lies in ruin. Its glory eroded and its purpose forever lost. The once-proud stone buildings crumble under the weight of time, while their unfortunate inhabitants - now cursed stone men - roam frozen in endless immortality.

When the heavens unleashed their wrath upon the north, a storm of magic and stone was cast into the skies, raining chaos across Erenshor. The depths of the planet itself became the rain and Rockshade Hold bore the brunt of this upheaval, absorbing an overwhelming surge of the strange ethereal material. The flesh of its monks, unprepared for such relentless magic, succumbed to its power.

Their transformation was slow but inevitable. Skin turned to stone, joints stiffened, and bodies became entombed in the dark rock of Erenshor itself. For some, the fiery chasms birthed by the impact offered merciful ends, consuming them before the curse could take hold. Yet, for those who sought refuge, survival became their cruelest fate - a self-preservation so complete that it forever denied them even the mercy of death.

These brothers, once devoted to recording the history of Erenshor and the divine bond between Brax and Sivakaya, found their dedication grotesquely immortalized. No longer able to grip the tools to write, to learn, or to reason, they now stand as statues - monuments to the history they so diligently studied. Bound by the enduring magic of Soluna’s Landing, they are trapped in this realm, their stony forms a reminder of their lost humanity.

Among the chaos, the invading magic gave rise to a monstrous being - a colossus of flame and fury. An embodiment of the darkness that had gathered over Rocksahde. It roared its dominion over the Hold, demanding fealty from its unintended subjects. The stone men, desperate for release, begged their molten master for mercy. But the giant, unyielding and vengeful, saw only servants in its creations. It demanded flesh as fuel, and so the stone men, once gentle historians, became unwilling hunters in service to their new king.

In their despair, the stone men turned their gaze to another. Their fading logic clung to a glimmer of hope - a name whispered in shadows and etched only by trembling hands: Azynthi. To this enigmatic figure, they gave words of desperate reverence: hope, praise, sacrifice. Perhaps he would help and so one was sent to find him but that tale ended in silence.

But beware the stone men of Rockshade Hold. They are no longer the scholars they once were, but hollow creatures, consumed by hatred and cursed with eternity. Their limbs, once graceful in the art of preservation, now move with heavy malice, driven by a rage born of suffering. They are history’s guardians no longer. They are monsters who threaten it.
